This is a press release from The Raya School

This January 2027, an authentic exhibition-atelier from Reggio Children will come to Manila, offering Filipino educators a rare opportunity to engage with the research, documentation, and pedagogical thinking developed in the infant-toddler centres and preschools of Reggio Emilia, Italy.

The Raya School, in partnership with Reggio Children and the Italian Embassy in Manila, will bring together more than 200 educators from across the Philippines for a roving exhibition and a two-day conference exploring the Reggio Emilia Approach to early childhood education.

Titled Mosaic of Marks, Words, Material, the exhibition explores research on mark-making and drawing woven with narrative. It reveals how children use materials, images, words, and multiple languages to express ideas, construct meaning, and make their thinking visible.

More than an exhibition, Mosaic of Marks, Words, Material invites educators to look closely at children’s work, listen deeply to their ideas, and reconsider how children learn, communicate, and express themselves.

The exhibition will open on January 21, 2027, at the Innovation Center of Miriam College, where it will run until February 3 before moving to another venue in Metro Manila. A two-day conference will take place on January 22–23, 2027, bringing educators into deeper dialogue with the Reggio Emilia Approach through the perspectives of two experienced practitioners from Reggio Emilia.

The conference will feature Moira Nicolosi and Marco Spaggiari, who will share their expertise with Philippine educators. Nicolosi has served as a Pedagogista in the Pedagogical Coordinating Team of the Istituzione of Preschools and Infant-toddler Centres of the Municipality of Reggio Emilia since 2014. Spaggiari, the conference Atelierista, will bring the perspective of the atelier, exploring the languages of materials, making, experimentation, and children’s creative expression.

Reggio Children is the institution recognized by the Municipality of Reggio Emilia and its preschools and infant-toddler centres to disseminate the Reggio Emilia educational philosophy internationally. Through the exhibition and conference, Philippine educators will have the opportunity to encounter this work directly and consider how its ideas might inform their own educational contexts and communities.

The event is open to early childhood educators, school leaders, pedagogical coordinators, atelieristas, art teachers, education students, Reggio-inspired practitioners, parents, and other advocates of child-centred education.

The Raya School is the best progressive school in Metro Manila dedicated to helping children discover themselves, their roots, and the world around them. Drawing on the Reggio Emilia philosophy, the school views each child as an individual with many languages—unique ways of understanding the world, communicating ideas, and expressing themselves creatively.

Through this partnership, The Raya School seeks to create opportunities for Philippine educators to engage with international perspectives on children’s learning and to reflect on how these ideas can enrich educational practice in their own communities.
